summary: Built step M1-S05 (type docs) for build tier2-webhook: the build-level package.xml aggregating every member of M1-S01 through M1-S04, and the compiled build-wide deploy-order note. The manifest carries 7 <types> blocks and 33 members at <version>67.0</version> with no wildcards: CustomObject x2 (including the platform event Tier2_Escalation__e), CustomField x13 (object-qualified, including Case.Tier2_Notified_At__c), ExternalCredential x1, NamedCredential x1, ApexClass x13, ApexTrigger x2, PermissionSet x1. The plan's inputs.members enumeration predates the M1-S03/M1-S04 rebuilds and names 11 ApexClass members; the artefacts on disk carry 13, because both Apex steps ship template-provenance copies (TestDataFactory in both, MockHttpResponseGenerator in M1-S03). TestDataFactory is emitted as ONE member, verified byte-identical across both steps and against templates/apex/tests/TestDataFactory.cls by SHA-256, discharging the open item in decision D-M1S03-06. Manifest-to-file consistency was verified in both directions: 33 members, 33 backing components, no member without a file and no artefact file without a member. The declared checker exits 0 with exactly the two WARN findings the plan predicted (ExternalCredential, NamedCredential on the risky-types list).
confidence_rationale: Step 10 MEDIUM: every element traced to the cited skill's fenced manifest example, the declared checker exited 0 on the first pass and check-outputs is ok, but the manifest membership had to be resolved against the artefacts on disk rather than from the plan's own inputs.members enumeration, which the M1-S03/M1-S04 rebuilds left two ApexClass members short, and the plan's inputs.deploy_order orders the PermissionSet before the fields it grants.

process_observations.observation: Every upstream step's deploy-order.md already named M1-S05 as the aggregator and stated what it must carry, so the member roll-up was read from the build's own record rather than re-derived from the raw file list.

The TestDataFactory duplication was flagged by both producing steps and recorded as a decision before this step ran, so the de-duplication was a discharge of a known open item rather than a discovery.

The plan's inputs.members.ApexClass for this step names 11 classes while the artefacts carry 13; the two template-provenance copies (TestDataFactory, MockHttpResponseGenerator) reached the build after the input was written and were never added to it.

The plan's inputs.deploy_order for this step places PermissionSet third, ahead of the object and field metadata its twelve fieldPermissions rows name, which is the ordering the cited skill's Anti-Pattern 4 and both upstream steps' notes say fails when the deploy is staged.

M1-S01 and M1-S02 each instruct that the other must not travel in the same deploy request, while the build-level manifest necessarily puts them in one; the cited gotcha's own remedy carries an 'unless the access change is the point of the deployment' carve-out and describes a retrieve-side hazard, which is why the combined request is written as safe here and the reasoning is recorded rather than assumed.

This step's own manual acceptance test still frames the AuthHeader parameterValue question in its pre-amendment form, which decision D-M1S02-06 records as the PV-007 prose lag; the narrowed reading is written into deploy-order.md section 3 step 1, but amend-step is refused now the step has left pending, so the plan text remains stale.

Both Apex steps recommend a dedicated Apex-foundations step to hold the shared template dependency and to restore the TriggerControl kill switch that remedy B dropped; that is a re-plan, not a file change.
process_observations.followup_reason: An Apex-foundations step is the structural fix for one template shared by two Apex steps and is where TriggerControl and Trigger_Setting__mdt would live.
